subject_ko: 평양 주재 소련대사관을 비롯해 영사관·통상대표부(Torgpredstvo)·국제서적기관(Mezhkniga)·전연방대외문화협회(VOKS)·타스(TASS)·소베트스키 베스트니크(Sovetskii Vestnik) 신문·해운회사(Mortrans)·대외무역은행(Vneshtorg Bank)·소련병원·소련중학교·수산무역기관(Rybvneshtorg)·MESTKOM·영화수출기관(Sovexportfilm)·항공협회(SOKAVA)·백화점(추린상회)까지 16개 소련계 기관의 인원과 직함을 열거한 첩보다. 지면을 새로 대조하니 이전 번역이 판독 불가로 남긴 인명·나이·직함·부서명 대다수가 지면에서 읽혔다.
key_points_ko: 평양 주재 소련대사관 대사는 테렌티 포미치 시티코프(Terenti Fomich Shtykov)다. 서기관은 제1서기관 펠류셴코(Pelyushenko), 제2서기관 트루빈(Trubin)이며, 그 밖에 페투호프(영어 통역)·모로조프(교육과장)·프로셴코(서기실장)·니키틴(OKR 방첩 대표)·레벤코(OKR 방첩 대표 겸 북조선 내무성 고문 보댜긴 대령과의 연락원)가 있다.

소련 영사관 총영사는 니콜라이 다닐로비치 프레디바일로(29세, 공산당 조직위원 겸임)이며, 통상대표부(Torgpredstvo) 대표는 트루소프(47세), 부대표는 세리코프(40세), 운전사는 크리벤코(MGB 모스크바와 연계되어 트루소프의 동정을 감시하는 것으로 여겨짐)다. 통상대표부 산하 부서장과 원산·청진·남양두만·함흥흥남 지점장 명단도 지면에서 새로 읽혔다.
6번 타스(TASS)와 8번 모르트란스(Mortrans) 사이에 이전 번역이 빠뜨렸던 「7. 소베트스키 베스트니크(Sovetskii Vestnik, 소련 통신)」 항목이 지면에서 온전히 확인되었다. 편집자는 카둘린으로, 소련 점령기 제25군 중좌 출신이다.
9~11번 항목(대외무역은행·소브볼니차·소베트스카야 시콜라)도 번호와 본문이 지면에서 또렷이 읽혀, 이전 번역이 「번호가 사라졌다」고 적었던 것과 달리 실제로는 번호가 살아 있었다.
SOKAVA(소련-조선 항공협회)는 1950년 6월 27일 평양 비행장이 폭격당해 항공기 20대 가운데 18대가 파괴되고 소련 국적자 12명이 죽었다고 적었다.
문서 끝의 논평(Comment)란은 이전에 보고된 인물 다섯(코발렌코, 모이세예프, 모로조프, 시티코프, 툰킨)을 정리했다. 그리고리 이바노비치 툰킨은 1945년 소련 외무성 극동국장을 지낸 고위 외교관으로 미소공동위원회 소련 측 수석 대표, 캐나다 왕립위원회의 소련 간첩 사건 보고서에 이름이 오른 인물이라고 적었다.

Director: Trusov, age about 47.
Deputy: Sikhon Timofeyevich Serikov, age 40.
Driver: Ivan Ivanovich Krivenko, age about 40, former major in the Soviet Army Tank Corps, believed to be directly linked with MGB Moscow for the purpose of reporting on Trusov's activities and behavior.

Department heads:
Chief bookkeeper: Vladimir Vasilyevich Semachin, age 19, who spent many years in Sinkiang.
Import (from USSR): Gubanov, age about 35.

Export (to USSR): Golovchanski, age about 43, veteran of the Soviet Army Tank Corps; right arm missing, presumably lost in World War II.

Materiel Inspector (Tovaroved): Amin, age about 42, and Ivleva, age about 37.

Legal Section: Bukreyev, age about 30.

Administrative and Supply Section (AKhO): Petrachenko, age about 37.

Branch managers: Wonsan, Zotov, age about 57.
Chongjin, Mikhalchenko, age about 35.
Namyang-Tumen, Kovalenko, age 40.
Hamhung-Hungnam, Panchenko, age about 56.

The main office of Torgpredstvo in Pyongyang had its own cipher communications system with Moscow, both by telephone and radio; there was also a direct telephone line to Hungnam. The communications office was in the main office building (Kanakura Building) near Songgyo-ri Bridge, on the third floor of the west wing.

Dalvneshtorg (Far East Foreign Trade Agency), a sub-division of Torgpredstvo, was managed by Serikov, deputy director of Torgpredstvo.

4. Mezhkniga (International Book Agency)

Honorary manager: Vladimir Vasilyevich Semakhin.
Executive manager: Varvara Ivanovna Golovina, age 36.

This agency was responsible for distributing Soviet books, periodicals, newspapers, and other printed matter in both Russian and Korean for propaganda purposes.

5. VOKS (All-Union Society of Cultural Relations)

The principal aims of this organization were to promote Soviet culture through the medium of various types of theatrical presentations. Personnel are unknown.

6. TASS (News Agency)

The manager was Kornilov; his wife was also in Pyongyang. Another employee, of unknown status, was Kotov, whose wife was also in Pyongyang.

7. Sovetskii Vestnik (Soviet Courier)

This Russian-language newspaper was typed (possibly mimeographed) and distributed through MESTKOM; its circulation is unknown. The editor, Kadulin, age about 57, was a lieutenant colonel in the 25th Army during the Soviet occupation, assigned to editing the paper. He remained in the same position as a civilian when the Soviet forces withdrew.

8. Mortrans (Soviet-Korean Marine Transport)

Director: Viktor Ivanovich Noiseyev, age 44.
Deputy director: Koltunov.

Chief of staff: Colonel Rosherski, age 44.

Principal: Radin, age 46.

12. Rybvneshtorg (Ministry of Marine Products)

Director: Pavel Lazarevich Shepshelevich, age 44.
Deputy: Mikhail Dekabetski, age 32; deported to the USSR in 1949 for living with a White Russian girl.

This organization is primarily engaged in conscription of Korean labor for the fishing industry in Kamchatka, Sakhalin, and other areas along the coast of the Maritime Provinces.

13. MESTKOM (performs the functions of the USSR trade union)

Chairman: Boris Ivanovich Smirnov, age 53, who maintained social control of the members of the Soviet colony and distributed the Russian-language newspaper.

14. Sovexportfilm (Soviet Film Export Agency)

Director: Boris Ivanovich Smirnov.

This agency had its own movie theaters throughout the larger cities of North Korea. It also supervised distribution of Soviet films to Korean theatres.

15. SOKAVA (Soviet Korean Air Association)

Director: Nosov, age about 53.

Preparations to establish this association were begun in January or February 1950, but operations were not under way until April. Its function was air passenger transportation for Koreans and Soviets, using twenty C-47 planes manned by Soviet crews. Pyongyang Central Airfield was the base of operations; the main office was located in the former U.S. liaison officer's house.

Flights were made from Pyongyang to Chongjin, Vladivostok, Dairen, Wonsan, Hamhung, and Mukden. Fares were very low, as for example, 1,500 won to

It was conjectured that the fares were set in anticipation of the "liberation" of South Korea, when, with surface transport disrupted, SOKAVA would be able immediately to provide cheap and attractive transportation to Seoul, Taegu, and Pusan, thus advancing the prestige of the USSR.

When the Pyongyang airfield was bombed on 27 June 1950, eighteen of the twenty SOKAVA planes were destroyed and twelve Soviet citizens were killed.

프로셴코(Proshchenko). 서기실장으로 여겨진다.

미상 직위: 우스티노프(Ustinov), 26세. 1950년 9월 모스크바에서 부임한 것으로 전해진다.
